purpose: E-BED §8.1 step 1: library cards P58 (decision table with hit policies), P59 (saga planner with reverse-order compensation and idempotent commands) and P60 (SLA / obligation clock with pause, resume and a business calendar), authored blind from outside sources and frozen before any spec-E is written or read.
digest: sha256 per file (raw bytes); card sha256 = sha256 of the lines "<path> <file sha256>\n" over the card's files in sorted path order; skeletonSha256 equals cards.mjs loadCard().skeletonSha256. Checked by experiments/library/test/ebed-cards.test.mjs.

notRead: research/enterprise-20261014/ (E-BED.md, BAR-SET, CATALOGUE and the rest)
blind.incidental: A grep for E-BED / G18 / P58 printed research/jit-20261008/PROOF-LEDGER.md lines 156-175 (claims L1-L12). They name P58 (decision table), P59 (compensation planner), P60 (obligation clock), the titles of E11 (Reg X), E12 (SEPA R-transactions) and E13 (payroll editions), and the phrase "effective-dated edition switches, new formats, schema renames and no-notice editions". No item specification, fixture or oracle was read. Nothing else under research/ about the bar set was opened.
blind.g18: The bar set's own definition of G18 was not read. The convention below is this author's, from the sources listed (Drools date-effective / date-expires as the precedent, with the case's business date in place of the wall clock).

rules: Editions are listed in increasing effectiveFrom and do not overlap; gaps are allowed; only the last edition may be open-ended. A malformed list is an invariant failure (the construction is wrong).
The edition is chosen by a business date taken from the case, never by the wall clock, so a replay decides the same way.
A case date that no edition covers deopts (guard ...-edition-in-force).
Every output names the edition(s) it applied.

perCard.P59: Not effective-dated: a saga instance is pinned to the definition VERSION it started on (Temporal-style versioning); an instance on another version deopts (guard definition-pinned).
perCard.P60: The policy edition (targets, warnings) in force on the clock's start date, local to the calendar, fixes the obligation's terms; the calendar edition (hours, holidays) is chosen per local day, so a clock running across a switch uses each day's hours.

runtime.note: P60 converts local business hours with Intl (the runtime tz database); its fixtures were hand-computed for Europe/London in October 2026 and checked on this runtime.
